release_notes.en-US: Improves how the extension decides whether two web addresses belong to the same site. Site boundaries now come from a Public Suffix List snapshot bundled inside the extension, so separately owned pages on a shared hosting service are treated as different sites and a misleading link between them is flagged instead of ignored. Country-code and other multi-part domain endings are also handled correctly. Permissions, data practices, and local-only analysis are unchanged.

version.approval_notes:
Version 0.1.6 replaces the registrable-domain approximation used for visible-domain mismatch detection. The previous logic recognized eleven shared-hosting providers and otherwise took the last two labels of a hostname, so two independently controlled tenants on any other provider collapsed to one site identity and the mismatch warning was suppressed. A security review reproduced this with two Blogspot tenants.

Site boundaries now come from a Public Suffix List snapshot committed at extension/psl-data.js, evaluated with the list's own algorithm including wildcard rules, exception rules, and the private section. That file is generated data rather than third-party executable code: it contains two newline-delimited string constants and no logic. tools/generate-psl.mjs in the repository regenerates it from https://publicsuffix.org/list/public_suffix_list.dat and reproduces the committed file byte for byte. Single-label rules are omitted because they yield the same result as the parser's default. The ICANN and private sections are stored separately because the private section alone identifies multi-tenant hosting, which the brand-impersonation check needs in order to keep recognizing official domains such as mail.google.com.

A seven-entry supplement in content.js covers multi-tenant platforms the list does not carry, including wordpress.com and glitch.me. Amazon S3 bucket-qualified hosts continue to resolve to the full host because bucket names may contain dots.

No permissions, data practices, network behavior, telemetry, or remote services changed. The list is consulted entirely on-device and no lookup leaves the browser; declared data collection remains none. Release workflow actions are now pinned to full commit SHAs. The repository test suite passes 27 tests, including new coverage for shared-hosting tenant separation, same-tenant links, multi-label registry suffixes, and ordinary same-site subdomains. Mozilla lint reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notices, and the package build succeeds.
